findings.title: Server response time (TTFB) is about 1.45 seconds
findings.explanation: The site took roughly 1450 ms just to start sending data back to the browser, before any page content even begins loading. No content delivery network (CDN) was detected in front of the site. Visitors, especially on mobile or slower connections, will perceive the site as slow, and slow load times can hurt search rankings and conversion rates.
findings.recommendation: Investigate what's causing the slow backend response (database queries, app logic, hosting resources) and consider adding a CDN or caching layer to speed up delivery.

findings.title: Response sent with 'no-store' caching directive
findings.explanation: The site's response headers tell browsers and intermediaries never to cache the page. Combined with the slow response time, this means every visitor pays the full cost of generating the page from scratch, with no ability to serve a cached copy faster.
findings.recommendation: Review whether 'no-store' is intentional; if the page content doesn't change per-request, use a more permissive caching policy to reduce load times and server load.

findings.title: TLS certificate expires in 60 days
findings.explanation: The site's SSL/TLS certificate, issued by Let's Encrypt, is valid and using modern TLS 1.3, but it has 60 days remaining before it expires. This is a routine informational note rather than an urgent issue, since Let's Encrypt certificates are typically renewed automatically.
findings.recommendation: Confirm automatic renewal is configured for the certificate so it doesn't lapse unexpectedly.

findings.title: SPF and DMARC records are configured
findings.explanation: The domain has both an SPF record (set to hard-fail unauthorized senders) and a DMARC record (set to quarantine policy). This helps prevent attackers from spoofing emails that appear to come from this domain, protecting both the business and its customers from phishing.
findings.recommendation: No action needed; consider tightening DMARC policy to 'reject' over time as confidence in mail flow grows.
